title: Nepal-China flood victims’ families given repayment deferments - Free Malaysia Today
description: Nepal-China flood victims’ families given repayment deferments  Free Malaysia Today
publisher.title: Free Malaysia Today
full_article:
Bank Negara Malaysia said families of the Nepal flood victims could reach out to their respective financial institution if they need further assistance. (EPA Images pic)

KUALA LUMPUR : Repayment deferments have since been extended to the families of victims of the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, says Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).

In a statement today, the central bank said relevant banks and insurance and takaful operators (ITOs) had engaged with the affected families following BNM’s meeting with the victims’ next of kin on Oct 12.

“Depending on the specific circumstances of the affected families, banks and ITOs are also considering further assistance, such as waivers of selected fees and charges, protection of customer assets and deposits, and facilitation of insurance/takaful claims.

“Affected families are encouraged to continue engaging directly with their respective banks and ITOs. Should they require further assistance or clarification, they may reach out to their respective financial institution,” BNM said.

BNM and the financial industry reiterated their readiness to extend appropriate relief and support to the victims’ families, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.

The central bank said it would continue to monitor the progress of these efforts.

On Aug 26, flash floods and landslides hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the area near its border with Tibet after heavy rain.

The next of kin of the 54 missing Malaysians have submitted a structured financial rescue plan to BNM, while the Nepali government works on legal changes to expedite their death certificates.

title: Rain possible in some parts of Nepal next week: Meteorologist - Khabarhub
description: Rain possible in some parts of Nepal next week: Meteorologist  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has urged the public not to panic over reports circulating on social media about a week-long spell of rainfall, saying rain is possible in some parts of the country from next Tuesday, but its extent and duration remain uncertain.

Meteorologist Rajan Maharjan of the Weather Forecasting Division said the weather system was changeable and it was too early to determine exactly where rainfall would occur, how much rain could fall and how long it would last.

He said farmers had been particularly concerned by social media reports claiming that rainfall would continue for an entire week.

“There is a possibility of rain from next Tuesday. However, it is not yet certain where it will rain, how much rainfall there will be or how long it will continue,” Maharjan said, urging the public not to believe unverified reports or become unnecessarily alarmed.

According to Maharjan, weather forecasts for Nepal are generally more reliable over a period of around three days, while predictions for an entire week remain less certain.

He said the department would provide more detailed information about the likelihood of rainfall in the coming week in the next few days.

Maharjan also urged the public, particularly farmers concerned about the potential impact on agricultural activities, to rely on official weather bulletins issued by the department rather than unverified claims circulating on social media.

Synopsis: India ranked 100th among 122 countries in the 2026 Global Hunger Index, with a score of 24.1, placing it in the “serious” category. Its score improved by just 1.7 points between 2018 and 2026, compared with an 8.2-point improvement between 2006 and 2012, while child wasting remained at 19%, the highest rate in South Asia.

India ranked 100th among 122 countries in the 2026 Global Hunger Index (GHI), with a score of 24.1, placing it in the “serious” hunger category. Published by German aid agency Welthungerhilfe (WHH) and Irish organisation Concern Worldwide, the index measures hunger and undernutrition across countries and tracks progress and setbacks. The 2026 edition draws on data from 2021 to 2025.

The GHI uses a 100-point scale, with lower scores indicating less hunger. Scores from 10 to 19.9 fall in the “moderate” category, while those from 20 to 34.9 are classified as “serious”.

India’s GHI score fell from 38.1 in 2000 to 24.1 in 2026, with 9.8 percent of the population being undernourished. More significantly, the score declined by just 1.7 points between 2018 and 2026, compared with an 8.2-point drop between 2006 and 2012.

“India’s GHI score, considered serious since 2012, mirrors the regional slowdown, with the score easing from 25.8 in 2018 to 24.1 in 2026,” the report said. It added that this “represents a fraction of its steep improvement of 8.2 points between 2006 and 2012.”

The GHI is based on four indicators: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting and child mortality.

Undernourishment fell to 9.8 percent in 2026. Child wasting, however, stood at 19 percent—the highest rate in the region—and remained high across all the reference years examined in the report. Wasting occurs when children under five weigh too little for their height and is usually a sign of acute undernutrition.

The report also accounts for factors associated with undernutrition, including poor diet quality, infections, and inadequate access to health services, safe water and sanitation.

Stunting, which reflects chronic undernutrition, fell to 29.3 percent in 2026, moving India from the “very high” to the “high” category for the first time. Child mortality also fell, with the share of children dying before their fifth birthday dropping from 9.2 percent in 2000 to 2.7 percent in 2026.

India trails Bangladesh on child wasting and stunting

India has also fared worse than its South Asian neighbours.

Nepal’s score fell from 18.4 in 2018 to 14.5 in 2026, an improvement of 3.9 points — more than twice the 1.7-point decline in India’s score. Sri Lanka’s score dropped from 11.4 to 10.2, while Bangladesh’s fell from 20.0 to 19.2, placing both countries in the “moderate” hunger category.

Pakistan’s score rose from 24.0 in 2018 to 25.5 in 2026. It ranked 106th, below India, which scored 24.1 and remained in the “serious” category.

The gap with Bangladesh is particularly stark in child nutrition. Child wasting stands at 19 percent in India, compared with 12.9 percent in Bangladesh. Bangladesh also has lower rates of stunting, at 24 percent, and undernourishment, at 8.2 percent.

India has a lower under-five mortality rate than both Bangladesh and Pakistan. The share of children who die before their fifth birthday is 2.7 percent in India, compared with 3 percent in Bangladesh and 5.6 percent in Pakistan.

Union government’s disputes hunger index

The Union government has previously rejected the Global Hunger Index (GHI), calling it “a deeply flawed measure of ‘Hunger’” that “does not reflect India’s true position”.

Savitri Thakur, Minister of State for Women and Child Development, told the Rajya Sabha on 5 August 2026, that the index “is a private construct published by 3 Non Government Organizations.”

Three of the index’s four indicators, Thakur said, “are actually related to health and nourishment levels in children” and “do not reflect prevalence of hunger in the overall population.” She also questioned the fourth indicator, which measures undernourishment across the population, saying it “suffers from significant methodological and data limitations”. The methodology, she added, “is unreliable and it cannot be taken to reflect hunger in the overall population.”

Thakur cited government food and nutrition schemes in support of the government’s position. The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana “substantially supplements the food requirements of up to 75% of the rural and up to 50% of the urban population”, she said. About 79.09 crore people receive free grain under the scheme.

The PM POSHAN scheme covers about 11.20 crore children in 10.36 lakh schools. Mission Poshan 2.0 addresses malnutrition through “cross cutting convergence amongst more than 18 Ministries/Departments”, she said. She also cited National Family Health Survey findings showing improvements in child malnutrition indicators across India.

The GHI report says its four indicators measure distinct aspects of hunger. Undernourishment “captures the food access situation of the population as a whole”, while the child indicators assess nutritional deficiencies among “a particularly vulnerable subset of the population”.

A lack of dietary energy, protein or micronutrients in children “leads to a high risk of illness, poor physical and cognitive development, and death”, the report says. It adds that combining the indicators reduces the effect of measurement errors.

In the first extraordinary meeting since its launch in 2022, the fund's board agreed to earmark the modest sum for the Himalayan country, which was hit in August by tsunami-like floods triggered by a climate-induced ice and rock avalanche that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.

title: Nepal to get $20 mn from Loss and Damage Fund. It covers just 0.7% of flood losses - ThePrint
description: Nepal to get $20 mn from Loss and Damage Fund. It covers just 0.7% of flood losses  ThePrint
publisher.title: ThePrint
full_article:
Nepal has not yet received the money. The Board’s decision to set aside the funds is the first step towards disbursing the assistance.

The $20 million allocation would cover just 0.7 per cent of Nepal’s estimated losses from the 26 August floods in Bhotekoshi River, according to Carbon Brief. However, the Board’s earlier decision established a maximum allocation of $20 million for an individual project or funding request under the mechanism through which Nepal’s request was made.

“Today the Loss and Damage Fund took a historic first step by responding to Nepal, but this cannot be a one-off,” said Harjeet Singh, global convenor of the Fill the Fund campaign. “We must set up a permanent rapid-response system that moves support in days, not months.”

The Loss and Damage Fund has received pledges totalling more than $800 million from 27 countries.

Nepal’s request, submitted on 31 August, less than a week after devastating floods struck the Himalayan country’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, received broad support at the FRLD meeting on Thursday. Fourteen Board members representing least developed countries, African states and Asia-Pacific states backed the request and called for an emergency meeting to address it.

Other blocs, including Latin American countries, Caribbean countries and small island developing states (SIDS), also called for an urgent response from the Board. Developed countries, meanwhile, endorsed holding consultations within the existing Loss and Damage Fund framework.

Since its inception, the Loss and Damage Fund has not disbursed any money to countries, although several project proposals are awaiting approval. Nepal’s request marks a significant moment because it is the first time the Board has agreed to set aside funds specifically for a sudden-onset disaster under the Barbados Implementation Modalities.

“The Loss and Damage Fund Board’s approval of $20 million for Nepal’s flood response shows that when countries come together, they can reach swift, effective consensus to address the urgent needs of vulnerable countries,” said Raju Chhetri, lead climate finance negotiator for the least developed countries at the UNFCCC, in a press release.

(Edited by Prashant Dixit)

full_article:
The Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has approved a $20 million (approximately Rs3 billion) allocation to Nepal to support relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction in communities devastated by floods in the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli region.

Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment Gita Chaudhary and Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle wrote to the fund on August 31, seeking urgent assistance for flood-affected communities. At a special meeting on Thursday, the fund’s board agreed to provide the funding.

The floods that struck the region on August 26 caused extensive damage and loss of life. Preliminary estimates indicate that more than 60,000 people from around 15,000 households were directly affected. Around 1,500 people reportedly lost their lives, while more than 5,000 remain missing.

full_article:
KATHMANDU: Khabarhub brings you a glimpse of major developments of the day in Nepal, including politics, business/economy, sports, entertainment, and more.

Nepal steps up preparations for COP31 climate summit

Nepal has intensified preparations for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled to take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Nepal’s position paper for the global climate summit is nearing completion. The ministry is collecting feedback and submissions from relevant stakeholders to refine the document before its finalization. Joint Secretary Dr. Maheshwor Dhakal, chief of the ministry’s Climate Management Division, said the position paper is expected to be unveiled next week. Nepal aims to strengthen its diplomatic efforts at the conference to advance climate justice and secure greater access to international climate finance.

UML senior leader Bidya Bhandari leaves for China to attend Global Governance Forum

Former President and senior CPN-UML leader Bidya Devi Bhandari departed for China on Thursday to participate in the Global Governance Forum scheduled to take place from October 23 to 25. The forum will be held in Xiong’an, Hubei Province, China, under the theme “Rebuilding Trust and Cooperation in a Changing World.” According to Bhandari’s secretariat, she is scheduled to address the gathering as a special guest. The visit marks Bhandari’s first foreign trip since her return to active politics as a senior leader of the CPN-UML. The three-day forum will feature parallel sessions, panel discussions and roundtable meetings on October 24 and 25, focusing on major global political, economic and environmental challenges. Discussions will cover the protection of the United Nations-centred international system, reforms in global peace and peacekeeping, the promotion of multilateralism, and the growing role of developing countries in international relations.

Nepal to host ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier Playoff

Nepal will host the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier Playoff from December 4 to 21, the Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) has announced. The tournament will feature eight teams: the bottom four teams from the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup League 2, along with the top two teams each from ICC Cricket World Cup Challenge League A and B. The top four teams from the playoff will advance to the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier, keeping their hopes of securing a place in the One-Day International (ODI) World Cup alive. Nepal will have an opportunity to reach the World Cup Qualifier for the second consecutive time through the tournament. Meanwhile, Nepal’s scheduled cricket series against India A will be affected by the hosting of the international competition and will no longer take place according to the previously planned schedule.

ICC grants List A T20 Status to all NPL matches

All matches of the third edition of the Nepal Premier League (NPL) have been granted official List A T20 status by the International Cricket Council (ICC), marking a significant milestone for domestic cricket in Nepal. The Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) announced the recognition on Wednesday, saying the ICC status would help strengthen the country’s cricketing structure and support the sport’s continued professionalization. The third edition of the NPL is scheduled to take place from October 26 to November 21, 2026, at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur. According to CAN, the recognition is expected to enhance the tournament’s credibility and raise the international profile of Nepali cricket. Official List A status also places the league’s matches within the recognized framework of limited-overs cricket, potentially adding greater significance to performances by participating players.

3,585 passengers benefit from free Nepal Police, APF bus services during Dashain

A total of 3,585 passengers benefited from free bus services operated by Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force (APF) in the Kathmandu Valley during the Dashain festival. According to Nepal Police Headquarters, three vehicles operated by Nepal Police provided free transportation to 1,406 passengers on October 20 and 21. Similarly, APF buses transported 2,179 passengers free of charge over three days beginning October 19, said Shailendra Thapa, deputy spokesperson for the force. The APF operated two buses in the Kathmandu Valley on Maha Ashtami, Maha Nawami and Bijaya Dashami to help passengers reach their destinations during the festive period. The free transportation services were introduced to ease travel for the public amid a shortage of public vehicles during Dashain, when many people travel to celebrate the festival with their families.

Nepali national among two killed by drone debris at Saudi Arabila oil facility

A Nepali national and a Filipino national were killed after debris from an intercepted drone struck an oil processing and production facility operated by Saudi Aramco in Saudi Arabia, according to the Saudi Ministry of Energy. An Indian national and a Pakistani national were also injured in the incident, which occurred on Wednesday. According to the Ministry, the drone was targeting the Shaybah oil field near the border with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) but was intercepted before reaching its target. Falling debris subsequently damaged the oil facility and sparked a fire in a vehicle belonging to a contractor working at the site. The ministry did not identify those responsible for launching the drone. However, Yemen’s Houthi rebels have carried out attacks targeting Saudi Arabia in the past.

Floods and landslides disrupt highways in Gandaki and Karnali provinces

Road traffic has been disrupted in several parts of Gandaki and Karnali provinces due to floods and landslides, Nepal Police said. The Beni-Jomsom road section in Myagdi district is operating on a one-way basis following a landslide at Baisari in Raghuganga Rural Municipality-2. Similarly, floods have obstructed roads in Arughat Rural Municipality-2, -3 and -4, as well as the Nayapul area of Gorkha district. According to police, the road connecting Arughat with Dharche has been completely blocked after an iron bridge at Sotigaun was swept away. Traffic has also been affected by flooding at Nayapul in Arughat Rural Municipality-1, where only small vehicles are currently able to operate. In Karnali Province, the Karnali Highway is operating on a one-way basis following a landslide at Oilise in Barahatal Rural Municipality-5, Surkhet.

Rain possible in some parts of Nepal next week: Meteorologist

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has urged the public not to panic over reports circulating on social media about a week-long spell of rainfall, saying rain is possible in some parts of the country from next Tuesday, but its extent and duration remain uncertain. Meteorologist Rajan Maharjan of the Weather Forecasting Division said the weather system was changeable and it was too early to determine exactly where rainfall would occur, how much rain could fall and how long it would last. He said farmers had been particularly concerned by social media reports claiming that rainfall would continue for an entire week. “There is a possibility of rain from next Tuesday. However, it is not yet certain where it will rain, how much rainfall there will be or how long it will continue,” Maharjan said, urging the public not to believe unverified reports or become unnecessarily alarmed.

Father and son killed in motorcycle accident in Arghakhanchi

A 62-year-old man and his 23-year-old son died after their motorcycle crashed in Bhumikasthan Municipality-2 of Arghakhanchi district last night. The victims died on the spot when the motorcycle, bearing registration number LU 64 P 7471, met with an accident, according to police. Deputy Superintendent of Police Diwas GC of the District Police Office, Arghakhanchi, confirmed the deaths, identifying the victims as Deviram Acharya, 62, and his 23-year-old son. Police said further investigation into the incident is underway to determine the circumstances that led to the crash.

Nepali Army officer strengthens women’s role in UN Peacekeeping

Lieutenant Colonel Rabin Thapa of the Nepali Army promoted the active participation of women peacekeepers in patrols, armed escorts and civilian protection missions while serving as a contingent commander with the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). Thapa emphasized the need to expand women peacekeepers’ involvement in operational assignments and strengthen engagement with local communities, particularly women and girls affected by conflict. Under his leadership, women peacekeepers participated in community outreach, emergency response and other security operations. Their involvement helped the battalion gain a better understanding of local security challenges and the protection needs of vulnerable communities. During periods of heightened insecurity, thousands of civilians sought refuge near United Nations bases following outbreaks of violence. In response, the battalion intensified patrols and strengthened civilian protection measures amid the deteriorating security situation.

Four suspension bridges to be rebuilt under Tanahun Hydropower Project

Four suspension bridges that will be affected by the reservoir of the 140-megawatt Tanahun Hydropower Project under construction in Tanahun district are set to be reconstructed. Tanahun Hydropower Limited has signed a contract agreement with Thani Kali Joshi Joint Venture (JV), Kathmandu, for the rehabilitation and reconstruction of the bridges affected by the project’s reservoir. Project Chief Shyamji Bhandari said the contract was awarded for Rs. 1,697,038, excluding taxes. According to Bhandari, the four bridges will be rebuilt at suitable locations identified in consultation with local residents. The necessary construction equipment and materials have also been supplied for the work. The bridges will be constructed in Chulesi, Tunibote, Dablyang and Tutuwa. The existing structures will be affected by the rising water level once the project reservoir comes into operation, making it necessary to relocate and rebuild them.

Nepal sees post-monsoon weather, mountain snowfall likely

Nepal is experiencing post-monsoon weather conditions, with westerly winds also influencing the country’s weather patterns. According to the latest bulletin issued by the Weather Forecasting Division, the hilly and mountainous regions are experiencing partly cloudy conditions, while most parts of the Terai are expected to remain generally clear. The Division has also forecast the possibility of light rainfall and snowfall at a few places in the mountainous regions. Weather conditions may vary across the country due to differences in terrain and atmospheric influences. While the Terai is likely to experience relatively clear skies, residents in the hills and mountains may see increased cloud cover, with a chance of precipitation in some high-altitude areas.

Kathmandu Valley’s minimum temperature drops to 13.5°C

Kathmandu Valley’s initial minimum temperature fell to 13.5 degrees Celsius on Thursday morning, down from 14.2 degrees Celsius recorded at the same time a day earlier, according to the Weather Forecasting Division. The temperature was recorded during the Division’s initial observation at 5:45 am on Thursday, indicating a decline of 0.7 degrees Celsius compared with Wednesday’s early-morning reading. However, the valley’s final minimum temperature on Wednesday was also recorded at 13.5 degrees Celsius, according to the division. The final reading is taken at 8:45 am, meaning the initial measurement may differ from the day’s officially recorded minimum temperature. The final minimum temperature for Thursday is expected to be confirmed after the scheduled 8:45 am observation.

Seven houses gutted in fire in Banke

Seven houses were destroyed in a fire suspected to have been caused by an electrical short circuit in Kapasi, Janaki Rural Municipality-6, Banke district, on Wednesday afternoon. A window of another concrete house was also damaged in the incident. According to police, the fire broke out at the house of Iddu Khan at around 2:20 p.m. It was brought under control by 4 p.m. with the help of police personnel and fire engines from Kohalpur Municipality and Nepalgunj Sub-Metropolitan City. The blaze completely gutted single-storey thatched houses belonging to Sabir Khan, Iddu Khan, Firoz Khan and Jabir Khan. Similarly, single-storey houses with tin roofs owned by Jabed Khan, Sarnam Khan and Saurabh Khan were also reduced to ashes.

Fire at Banke Steel Factory causes damage worth Rs. 15.6 million

A fire broke out in a furnace oil tank at Ambe Steel Sariya Company in Bakaspur, Janaki Rural Municipality-5, Banke district, early Thursday, causing an estimated damage of Rs. 15.6 million. According to Deputy Superintendent of Police Prati Singh Rathore, information officer at the District Police Office, Banke, the fire started at around 1:30 am, reportedly due to an electrical short circuit in the furnace oil tank used in the steel production process. Following the incident, a police team from the Area Police Office in Khajurakhurd was dispatched to the site after receiving information about the fire. The blaze was brought completely under control within an hour through the joint efforts of Nepal Police personnel, local residents and firefighters, Rathore said.

Nepali team leaves for Western Asian Youth Chess Championship in India

A Nepali chess team has departed for Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India, to participate in the Western Asian Youth Chess Championship 2026, scheduled to run from October 22 to 31. Raju Tamrakar, spokesperson for the Nepal Chess Federation, bade farewell to the 18-member delegation at Tribhuvan International Airport on Thursday. The team is led by Nita Sainju, a member of the federation’s central committee, and comprises 11 players from different age categories, five guardians, a judge and other team members. The Nepali players competing in the championship include Sunab Ojha, Shubhang Pradhan, Agrim Sainju, Ayush Bhandari, Prabir KC, Agrata Acharya, Nihana Shrestha, Ujjibani Kandel and Nelisa Ojha. Prabish Prajapati will serve as the team’s judge.

Five killed in road accidents across Nepal in 24 hours

Five people have died in separate road accidents across the country in the past 24 hours, while 313 others have been injured in crashes reported in Kathmandu, Sunsari, Makawanpur, Morang and Tanahun districts, according to Nepal Police Headquarters.

Cardamom cultivation trial proves successful in Beni

Cardamom cultivation launched on a trial basis in Musung village of Beni Municipality-3, Myagdi, has proved successful, prompting farmers to expand production commercially. Padam Pun, chairperson of Beni Municipality-3, said more farmers had begun cultivating cardamom after plants grown in the forest area of Charkhola started producing well. The trial cultivation began three years ago. Cardamom is now being grown on more than 20 ropanis of land after bushes were cleared from barren and wetland areas. Favourable climatic conditions, suitable geography, market access, and attractive prices have encouraged farmers to take up the crop. Around 50 years ago, a landslide destroyed cultivable land in the area, leaving it barren. The success of cardamom farming has created new opportunities to bring such land back into productive use.

title: UN climate disaster fund moves to provide $20 mn aid for Nepal - Yahoo News Singapore

full_article:
The United Nations' climate loss and damage fund moved Thursday to provide $20 million in aid sought by flood-stricken Nepal, the first time it has set aside money for any country, in a key test of the body's credibility.

In its first extraordinary meeting, the fund's board agreed to earmark the modest sum for the Himalayan country, which was hit in August by tsunami-like floods triggered by a climate-induced ice and rock avalanche that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.

Camila Minerva Rodriguez Tavarez, the Dominican co-chair of the board, called the outcome "truly historic" and thanked members for "allowing us to act promptly and have a response to Nepal."

"It's a landmark first step. At the same time, it's also a proof of how far the fund still has to go," Harjeet Singh, founding director of the Satat Sampada Climate Foundation and global convenor of the Fill the Fund campaign, which has been pressuring the fund, told AFP.

The decision does not, however, mean that Nepal will immediately receive the funding, which amounts to less than 0.5 percent of the government's $4.78 billion estimate for reconstruction.

Twenty million dollars is the maximum amount countries can request in a single application.

The creation of the "Fund for responding to Loss and Damage" was hard-won at the UN climate conferences of 2022 and 2023 by developing countries, many of them among the least responsible for climate change yet most vulnerable to its impacts.

The fund grew out of calls for "climate reparations" from historically major emitters, which ultimately did not materialize.

But since it became operational, critics have faulted both meager pledges from rich nations -- $822 million to date -- and a disbursement cycle disconnected from climate disasters.

No money has been disbursed so far.

- Precedent tussle -

During the meeting, some developed countries stressed the Nepal decision should be seen as exceptional, not as a template for the fund's long-term future.

"This is not a precedent on one hand, but on the other it provides a learning for the development of the long-term model of the fund," the European Union's Jan Dusik said.

Developing countries hit back.

"I heard Jan saying that we are open for learning, but not in setting precedent. Please do not define the boundaries for learning," said Pakistan's Ali Tauqeer Sheikh, in comments endorsed by others.

Last year after part of Jamaica was destroyed by the worst hurricane in its history, the fund's French co-chair at the time told AFP that it was not meant to "provide a humanitarian response" but was aimed at "the next stage."

That wait-and-see approach became untenable after the disaster in Nepal. Developing countries, which hold a majority of the fund's board, demanded a response to Nepal's request.

- Legal obligations? -

"Nepal is actually driving us into how the fund is going to look like when it comes to rapid disbursement modalities," said Brenda Mwale, outreach lead at the Loss and Damage Collaboration.

The UN and its humanitarian partners launched a $49.6 million emergency appeal after the Nepal disaster, and the United States announced $31 million in new flood recovery support in September.

But as courts increasingly rule on states' climate obligations, developing countries and legal experts argue that such aid should be an obligation of rich countries, not voluntary.
